title: Insurance Denied Your Claim in Henderson
metaDescription: Insurance denied your Henderson crash claim? NV appeal steps, bad-faith basics, and documentation checklist.
excerpt: Educational Henderson, NV guide — 2-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: Confirm coverage at the scene
paragraphs: Ask for insurance card photos and verify policy status. In Henderson, uninsured motorist rates track with statewide averages — always assume minimum limits until verified.

sections.heading: Your UM/UIM policy in Nevada
paragraphs: Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage on your policy may pay when the at-fault driver has no coverage or insufficient 25/50/20 limits.
Notify your carrier promptly; UM claims still require documentation of injuries and damages.

sections.heading: Hit-and-run steps in Henderson
paragraphs: Report hit-and-runs immediately to Henderson police. UM coverage often requires a police report within 24–72 hours.
Seek witnesses and camera footage near High-traffic corridors in Henderson, NV.

sections.heading: Medical and financial documentation
paragraphs: Use Henderson area hospitals and emergency departments if injured. Track lost wages and transportation costs.

sections.heading: When litigation may be necessary
paragraphs: If UM/UIM carriers deny or lowball offers, a licensed Nevada attorney can evaluate bad-faith and negligence claims against the at-fault driver directly.

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my Henderson case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in Nevada?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 2-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.

faq.question: Will my rates increase if I use UM/UIM coverage?
faq.answer: Rules vary by carrier and state. Ask your insurer in writing; using UM after a not-at-fault crash is often protected — verify your policy.
